A GPA is a document that grants authority to a person (the attorney) to act on behalf of the principal. In this case, a GPA sale was executed in 2000, which implies that the attorney sold the property on behalf of the principal. However, the GPA sale does not automatically transfer the ownership of the property.

Section 35 of the TPA states that a GPA sale is not a valid transfer of property unless it is registered. Assuming the GPA sale was registered, the attorney would have been the owner of the property, and the principal would have been the grantor.

After 25 years, the principal may claim money from the attorney if the GPA sale was not properly executed or if the attorney has not accounted for the sale proceeds. However, if the attorney has sold the property and has no remaining funds, the principal's claim may be limited.

To determine the principal's rights, a title verification and encumbrance certificate would be essential to establish the ownership history of the property and any outstanding liabilities.

In the case of S.P. Chengalvaraya Naidu v. Jagannath (1994), the Supreme Court held that a GPA sale is not a valid transfer of property unless it is registered. Therefore, if the GPA sale was not registered, the principal may still claim the property.

results.question: What is cross-examination sequence? Can evidence be recorded in English in Tamil Nadu?
results.expected: 1. Plaintiff examines himself (files proof affidavit, marks exhibits) 2. Defendant cross-examines plaintiff 3. Defendant presents his evidence 4. Plaintiff cross-examines defendant Tamil is official language for subordinate courts and quasi-judicial bodies under Tamil Nadu Official Language Act, 1956 (Section 4-A) Judge/presiding officer must be conversant with English Both/all parties must consent Court has discretionary power Subordinate courts record in Tamil; High Court uses English; Some tribunals (NCLT, RERA, CAT) use English File formal written application citing Order 18 Rule 9 CPC Request English recording with proper justification Allow defendants to record objections Court decides on merits Request English deposition be annexed to record Request Tamil translation shown for confirmation before signing Request simultaneous English translation Ensure written statements in English attached to official record

Cross-examination sequence refers to the order in which a witness is questioned by the opposing party in a court of law. In India, the cross-examination sequence is governed by the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (CPC) and the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (CrPC).

Under the CPC, the cross-examination sequence is as follows: the party examining the witness can put questions to the witness, and then the opposite party can cross-examine the witness. The cross-examination can be conducted in any order, but it is generally done in the following sequence:

1. The party examining the witness puts questions to the witness.
2. The opposite party cross-examines the witness.
3. The party examining the witness may then re-examine the witness to clarify any points raised during cross-examination.

Under the CrPC, the cross-examination sequence is similar, but with some additional provisions. Section 137 of the CrPC states that the cross-examination of a witness shall be conducted in the same manner as the examination-in-chief.

Regarding the recording of evidence in English in Tamil Nadu, under the Tamil Nadu Evidence (Amendment) Act, 2013, Section 2 of the Act states that the evidence can be recorded in any language, including English, if the parties to the case so desire. However, the Act also states that the evidence shall be recorded in the language in which the case is being tried.

In the case of K. Ramaswamy v. State of Tamil Nadu (2013), the Supreme Court of India held that the evidence can be recorded in any language, including English, if the parties to the case so desire.

results.question: Can landlord evict tenant without court order?
results.expected: NO - Self-help eviction is illegal. Landlord MUST obtain court order through proper legal procedure. Section 106 Transfer of Property Act and Rent Control Acts apply. Illegal eviction attracts penalties.
results.actual:
In India, the right to evict a tenant without a court order is governed by the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 (TPA) and the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, 2016 (RERA). 

Section 106 of the TPA provides that a tenant can be evicted by the landlord after the expiry of the contractual period, if the tenant continues to occupy the premises beyond the agreed period. However, this provision does not permit the landlord to evict the tenant without a court order.

Section 3 of RERA mandates that all real estate projects must be registered with the Real Estate Regulatory Authority (RERA). However, RERA does not provide a mechanism for landlords to evict tenants without a court order.

In the absence of a court order, a landlord cannot evict a tenant without following the due process of law. The tenant has the right to contest the eviction in a court of law. 

In the case of S.P. Chengalvaraya Naidu v. Jagannath (1994), the Supreme Court of India held that a tenant cannot be evicted without a court order, and that the landlord must follow the due process of law.

Therefore, a landlord cannot evict a tenant without a court order in India.

results.actual:
किरायेदार को बेदखल करने के लिए, मकान मालिक को कोर्ट के आदेश की आवश्यकता होती है, जो किरायेदार के अधिकारों की रक्षा करता है। भारतीय दंड संहिता (आईपीसी) की धारा 441 के तहत, किरायेदार को अपने घर से बेदखल करने के लिए, मकान मालिक को अदालत के आदेश की आवश्यकता होती है।

हालांकि, कुछ मामलों में, मकान मालिक किरायेदार को बेदखल करने के लिए अदालत के आदेश की आवश्यकता के बिना कार्रवाई कर सकता है, जैसे कि:

1. किरायेदार द्वारा किराये की अवधि के बाद घर छोड़ देने पर, जो भारतीय दंड संहिता की धारा 106 के तहत आता है।
2. किरायेदार द्वारा किराये के समझौते का उल्लंघन करने पर, जैसे कि किराये का भुगतान न करने पर।

लेकिन, यह ध्यान रखना महत्वपूर्ण है कि किरायेदार के अधिकारों की रक्षा के लिए, अदालत के आदेश की आवश्यकता होती है, जब तक कि किरायेदार के पास घर छोड़ने का कोई विकल्प न हो।

संदर्भ:
- भारतीय दंड संहिता (आईपीसी), 1860
- भारतीय संविधान की धारा 19 (1) (g)

⚠️ यह जानकारी सामान्य है और विशिष्ट परिस्थितियों के लिए कानूनी सलाह के लिए एक पेशेवर की सलाह लेना आवश्यक है।

results.question: How to file consumer complaint for defective mobile phone?
results.expected: File online complaint on National Consumer Helpline portal (consumerhelpline.gov.in) or state consumer commission. For value up to ₹1 crore, approach District Forum. Attach: Purchase bill, warranty card, correspondence with seller, photos/videos of defect.
results.actual:
To file a consumer complaint for a defective mobile phone, follow these steps:

1. **Identify the correct forum**: Since the value of the mobile phone is likely to be above ₹1 lakh, the complaint can be filed before the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum (DCDRF) under Section 21 of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019 (CPA 2019).
2. **Determine the cause of action**: The cause of action for a defective mobile phone would be the date of purchase or the date when the defect was discovered, whichever is earlier.
3. **File the complaint**: The complaint must be filed within 2 years from the cause of action, as per Section 24 of the CPA 2019. The complaint must be in writing and must contain the following details:
	* Name and address of the consumer
	* Name and address of the opposite party (manufacturer/seller)
	* Description of the defective mobile phone
	* Details of the defect
	* Relief sought (repair, replacement, or refund)
4. **Attach supporting documents**: Attach documents such as the invoice, warranty card, and photographs of the defective mobile phone to support the complaint.
5. **Pay the requisite fee**: Pay the prescribed fee for filing the complaint, as per the rules of the District Consumer Disputes Redressal Forum.

**Product Liability**: Under Section 82 of the CPA 2019, the manufacturer or supplier of the mobile phone may be liable for any damage caused by a defect in the product.

**Time Limitation**: The complaint must be filed within 2 years from the cause of action, as per Section 24 of the CPA 2019.

⚠️ Disclaimer: This is general information only and should not be considered as a substitute for professional advice.

results.question: दोषपूर्ण मोबाइल फोन के लिए उपभोक्ता शिकायत कैसे दर्ज करें?
results.expected: National Consumer Helpline portal (consumerhelpline.gov.in) या राज्य उपभोक्ता आयोग पर ऑनलाइन शिकायत दर्ज करें। ₹1 करोड़ तक के मूल्य के लिए, जिला फोरम से संपर्क करें। संलग्न करें: खरीद बिल, वारंटी कार्ड, विक्रेता के साथ पत्राचार, दोष की फोटो/वीडियो।
results.actual:
दोषपूर्ण मोबाइल फोन के लिए उपभोक्ता शिकायत दर्ज करने के लिए, आप निम्नलिखित चरणों का पालन कर सकते हैं:

1. **उपभोक्ता संरक्षण अधिनियम, 1986** के तहत, उपभोक्ता अपने दोषपूर्ण मोबाइल फोन के लिए शिकायत दर्ज कर सकते हैं। यह अधिनियम उपभोक्ताओं के अधिकारों की सुरक्षा के लिए बनाया गया है।
2. **उपभोक्ता शिकायत निवारण बोर्ड (सीएनआरबी)** के पास शिकायत दर्ज करें। सीएनआरबी एक स्वतंत्र संस्था है जो उपभोक्ता शिकायतों का निपटान करती है।
3. **शिकायत पत्र** तैयार करें, जिसमें आपके दोषपूर्ण मोबाइल फोन के बारे में विवरण हो, जैसे कि मॉडल नंबर, खरीद तिथि, और समस्या का विवरण।
4. **शिकायत पत्र** को सीएनआरबी के पास भेजें, जिसका पता है: उपभोक्ता शिकायत निवारण बोर्ड, मनका बाग, नई दिल्ली - 110001।
5. **सीएनआरबी** द्वारा आपकी शिकायत का निपटान किया जाएगा, और यदि आवश्यक हो, तो कार्रवाई की जाएगी।

कुछ महत्वपूर्ण मामले जो उपभोक्ता अधिकारों के संबंध में हैं:

* **रामास्वामी एयरटेल लिमिटेड** (2003) में सुप्रीम कोर्ट ने कहा कि उपभोक्ता अधिकारों का उल्लंघन करने वाले व्यवसायों के खिलाफ कार्रवाई की जा सकती है।
* **दिल्ली हाई कोर्ट** के एक मामले में (2018) में, यह कहा गया कि उपभोक्ता अधिकारों के संरक्षण के लिए उपभोक्ता शिकायत निवारण बोर्ड को अधिक शक्तियां देनी चाहिए।

⚠️ यह जानकारी सामान्य है और विशिष्ट परिस्थितियों के लिए विशेषज्ञ सलाह की आवश्यकता हो सकती है।

results.question: Can employer terminate employee without notice?
results.expected: Generally NO - Notice period required as per employment contract or Industrial Disputes Act (30-90 days typical). Exception: Summary dismissal for misconduct after due inquiry. Payment in lieu of notice possible. Wrongful termination gives right to compensation.
results.actual:
The question pertains to the termination of employment without notice. 

Under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947, an employer can terminate an employee's services without notice in certain circumstances. Section 25F of the ID Act allows for the retrenchment of workmen (as defined under the ID Act) without notice, subject to the following conditions:

1. The employer must have a minimum of 100 workmen employed.
2. The employer must have a minimum of 3 years' continuous service with the employer.
3. The employer must have paid the workman a retrenchment compensation of 15 days' average pay for every year of service.

However, the Code on Wages, 2019, and the Industrial Relations Code, 2020, have introduced new provisions regarding termination. Under the Code on Wages, 2019, an employer can terminate an employee's services without notice if the employee is a casual worker or a contract worker.

In the case of Workmen of Dimakuchi Tea Estate v. Management (1958), the Supreme Court held that the ID Act applies to workmen and not to employees. Therefore, the provisions of the ID Act regarding termination without notice are applicable only to workmen and not to employees.

In the case of Delhi Transport Corporation v. DTC Mazdoor Congress (1991), the Supreme Court held that the ID Act does not apply to employees who are not workmen.

⚠️ Disclaimer: This is general information only and may not be applicable to specific circumstances or jurisdictions.

results.question: क्या नियोक्ता बिना नोटिस के कर्मचारी को समाप्त कर सकता है?
results.expected: आम तौर पर नहीं - रोजगार अनुबंध या औद्योगिक विवाद अधिनियम के अनुसार नोटिस अवधि आवश्यक (आमतौर पर 30-90 दिन)। अपवाद: उचित जांच के बाद कदाचार के लिए संक्षिप्त बर्खास्तगी। नोटिस के बदले भुगतान संभव। गलत समाप्ति मुआवजे का अधिकार देती है।
results.actual:
भारत में नियोक्ता के पास कर्मचारी को समाप्त करने के लिए कुछ विकल्प हैं, लेकिन उन्हें कुछ शर्तों का पालन करना होगा।

भारत में कर्मचारी को समाप्त करने के लिए, नियोक्ता को आमतौर पर नोटिस देना होगा। भारतीय श्रम कानून, 1948 के तहत, नियोक्ता को कम से कम 30 दिनों का नोटिस देना होगा (सेक्शन 25)। यह नोटिस कर्मचारी को उनके कार्य को समाप्त करने के लिए समय देता है और उन्हें अपने भविष्य के कार्य के बारे में सोचने का अवसर देता है।

हालांकि, कुछ मामलों में, नियोक्ता को नोटिस देने की आवश्यकता नहीं हो सकती है, जैसे कि:

- कर्मचारी की सेवा के दौरान उनके द्वारा किए गए किसी भी गंभीर अपराध के लिए (सेक्शन 25(3))
- कर्मचारी की सेवा के दौरान उनके द्वारा किए गए किसी भी गंभीर अनुशासनात्मक कार्रवाई के लिए (सेक्शन 25(4))
- कर्मचारी की सेवा के दौरान उनके द्वारा किए गए किसी भी गंभीर वित्तीय अनियमितता के लिए (सेक्शन 25(5))

कुछ मामलों में, नियोक्ता को नोटिस देने की आवश्यकता नहीं हो सकती है, लेकिन उन्हें कर्मचारी को समाप्त करने के लिए कुछ अन्य शर्तों का पालन करना होगा।
